newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks to test record high after HSBC results.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks to test record high after HSBC results.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to test record levels on Tuesday, with brokers predicting gains of 100 to 200 points on the Hang Seng Index, propelled by a rally in HSBC Holdings after it posted strong interim earnings.
"The Hang Seng Index will open up 150 points due to the strength of HSBC overnight as well as its results," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
"The focus will be on the banking sector today," he added.
HSBC reported a 13 percent rise in pretax profit for the first six months of the year to 2.62 billion sterling.
Profit attributable to shareholders was HK$22.22 billion.
The stock made sharp gains in London overnight, rising to a high of HK$279 before closing at HK$271.75 and pushing the Hang Seng London Reference Index 145.54 points higher to 16,405.13.
The Hang Seng Index fell 119.63 points on Monday to close at 16,259.59 on Monday. The record high stands at 16,449.53.
Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities, said banks had benefited from a sharp run recently so the upside could be limited.
"Even though the banking stocks will be the focus, I don't expect too much upside after the recent rally," he said.
He saw near-term resistance at 16,800 points for the Hang Seng Index.
